candidates: Progressive Ataxia and Palatal Tremor (PAPT), sporadic type
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast
champion: Progressive Ataxia and Palatal Tremor (PAPT), sporadic type

raw.champion: Progressive Ataxia and Palatal Tremor (PAPT), sporadic type
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive ataxia, palatal myoclonus, and severe cerebellar atrophy on MRI, along with the absence of genetic mutations for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12, supports the diagnosis of PAPT, sporadic type.

rejected.label: Sporadic Adult-Onset Ataxia (SAOA)
rejected.why: SAOA is a broader category and does not specifically account for the palatal myoclonus and severe cerebellar atrophy seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Idiopathic late-onset cerebellar ataxia
rejected.why: This diagnosis is too nonspecific and does not capture the unique combination of symptoms, including palatal myoclonus, presented by the patient.

rejected.label: Multiple System Atrophy
rejected.why: While MSA can present with ataxia and cerebellar atrophy, the patient's lack of prominent autonomic dysfunction and parkinsonian features, along with the presence of palatal myoclonus, makes PAPT a more fitting diagnosis.
